explanation: In 1291 Venice ordered its glass furnaces onto Murano, partly to keep fire away from the city's wooden buildings. Lace is the speciality of neighbouring Burano.

claims.text: Murano, an island in the Venetian Lagoon, has been famous for glassmaking since the late 13th century.
Murano is not chiefly known for lace-making, mask-making or boatbuilding.
In 1291 the Republic of Venice ordered glassmakers to move their furnaces to Murano, partly because of the fire risk to the city.
The neighbouring lagoon island of Burano is famous for lace.
